column1: All numbers would have an extra zero at the end, but nothing else would change. Your economic well-being depends on relative prices, not the overall price level. Why, then, is a persistent increase in the price level a social problem? It turns out that the costs of inflation are subtle. Indeed, economists disagree about the size of the social costs. To the surprise of many laymen, some economists argue that the costs of inflation are small—at least for the moderate rates of inflation that most countries have experienced in recent years.
